rules: Frame 0 is a satellite map already moving (zoom-in or pan), never a still or a title card; narration and the first caption start at 0.0-0.2 s, first pin or card by 1.5 s.

Open with a geographical paradox, visual pun (e.g. Chili -> Chile), stark dividing line (80% vs 20%, Wallace Line, 24 time zones), impossible barrier (Darien Gap, Gibraltar 14 km, Tibet no-fly zone), or magnifying-glass mystery (? ? ?).

Use HyperFrames scenes as the primary visual composer (satellite map, historical parchment map, 2D side-view cross-section diagram, 3D space globe, Google Earth 3D horizon profile, cards, and props). Move between places on one map with a continuous camera path (zoom-out -> pan -> deep zoom-in up to 16x) or cut freely whenever the narrative rhythm calls for a new shot.
The camera never holds still: continuous drift >= 0.06 ln/s between camera moves, no hold over 1.7 s (hard limit 3.0 s), with 3D pitch/tilt on terrain barriers and close-up beats.
Something new on screen every 1-3 s: a pin, a region fill, a white-bordered cutout sticker, a flag-character, a dashed distance or dimension bar, an animated counter, a route segment, or a new shot.

Typography follows surface mode: clean geometric sans-serif (Inter Bold / SemiBold / Archivo Black) on dark satellite, 3D globe, radar, and cross-section scenes (ALL CAPS for macro countries/mountains, Title Case for features/cities/peaks, yellow initial-letter highlights for acronyms like NAT or UTC), and serif/engraved type (EB Garamond / Playfair Display / Cinzel) strictly on historical parchment or blueprint maps.

Prove scale visually using true-scale country polygon dragging (e.g. Chile stretched from London to Baghdad), polygon tiling (5x France inside Tibet), everyday object scale cutouts (Costco parking lot beside Market Island), or engineering dimension bars (mi + km).

Use 2D side-view cross-section diagrams when explaining underwater depth (900 m Gibraltar vs 75 m Channel Tunnel, Wallace trench), soil/root layers, or vertical dust walls, and 3D horizon profiles for mountain/flight altitude comparisons (33,000 ft vs 14,800 ft).

Distinguish territories clearly using translucent entity fills with glowing borders, diagonal striped fills (45 deg) for split zones, physical surface textures (cracked earth, 3D trees), full waving flag-map fills, or animated flag-characters.

Captions stay at fixed y = 1382 (bottom <= 1480 px, Shorts safe zone), Inter Bold 84 px white, 1-2 words per event, no outline, soft drop shadow, no per-word highlight and no box by default (a box is a deliberate choice, not blocked).
Watermark 'Geoverum' stays clear at the watermark top right (32 px clearance).
Music and SFX come from Epidemic Sound only, mixed to -14.0 LUFS (-1.5 dBTP) with music ducked -12 dB under the voiceover and no silence gap over 0.65 s.
The last 5 s return to a keyword or title from the hook on screen (or an icon equation / 3D globe / real aerial photo payoff); No call to action and no end card.

liked.what: continuous multi-stop camera path across one map or dynamic cuts that follow narrative beats
liked.why: preserves spatial orientation from macro continent scale down to 16x enclave/island close-ups while keeping pacing flexible

liked.what: year or hero percentage held big and clean before supporting pill badges appear
liked.why: one clear focal point per beat without competing text

liked.what: geographical paradox hook with an instant dividing line, visual pun, or magnifying-glass mystery in the first 1.5 s
liked.why: immediately hooks viewer curiosity with a visual contradiction (Market zigzag, Chili->Chile, Tibet flight void, Gibraltar bridge ?)

liked.what: true-scale polygon drag, polygon tiling, or everyday object scale comparison (Chile over London-Baghdad, 5x France in Tibet, Costco lot next to Market Island)
liked.why: turns abstract area and length numbers into an unforgettable visual comparison

liked.what: 2D side-view cross-section diagram and 3D horizon altitude profile (900 m Gibraltar vs 75 m Channel Tunnel, Wallace trench, 33,000 ft plane over Himalayas, prairie roots)
liked.why: makes vertical depth, underwater geology, and flight altitude barriers immediately clear

liked.what: white-bordered cutout stickers (animals, tractors, ships, planes) and interactive tool props (magnifying glass, pencil redrawing border, crossed-out badges)
liked.why: adds tactile motion and humor while keeping the map uncluttered

liked.what: icon equation summary ([Depth] + [Currents] + [Earthquakes] = $) or 3D globe core-to-summit radius comparison (+21 km, +2 km)
liked.why: crystallizes multi-factor engineering or geophysical explanations into a single visual punchline

liked.why: A/B 2026-11-01: 84 paling bersih, tidak menutupi peta, tetap terbaca di layar HP (Arundaya)

liked.what: segmen fleksibel mulai 0,8 s; bebas melakukan cut sesuai ritme narasi tanpa batas jumlah cut

rejected.what: static frame or camera hold over 1.7 s
rejected.why: violates P01/P02; the map or still must keep drifting

rejected.what: call to action or subscribe end card
rejected.why: Geoverum ends on the final factual twist or keyword return

rejected.what: unquantified geographic claims without a line, dimension bar, counter, pill badge, or scale overlay on screen
rejected.why: every spoken distance, depth, altitude, or area comparison must have a matching visual anchor

rejected.what: cluttered multi-line paragraphs or backing boxes on captions
